entries.subject: LAM/SPHERE MPCD: selected reconstruction
entries.finding: The current LAM 3Dshape directory lists 354_Eleonora_mpcd.obj, matching the actual preparation input. The retained measurements describe 2002 vertices and 4000 facets in km; the recipe preserves that source scale. This review checked the release listing and local source/recipe binding, not a fresh mesh reconstruction or new source-fit test.

entries.subject: Size and pole
entries.finding: The retained Table 1 and Table A.1 extract records diameter 165 km, ecliptic J2000 pole (154°, 24°), period 4.277185 h. Published survey diameter averages ADAM and MPCD; the released MPCD coordinates are not rescaled to that average. The measured source volume-equivalent radius is 81.87205994336064 km. These source interpretations were checked against the recipe; the paper table was not freshly re-transcribed in this pass.

entries.subject: Released SPHERE observations and surface registration
entries.finding: The live source folder https://observations.lam.fr/astero/Data/354Eleonora/ contains Deconv/ and Red/. Reduced and deconvolved observations therefore have a concrete archive route. Their pixels, image geometry, coverage and photometry were not qualified in this directory-level check, so these files cannot yet be treated as a registered global reflectance map. The current grid remains an explicit missing-imagery presentation.
entries.revisitWhen: The original image headers and publication establish a usable projection onto this specific MPCD model, and a native-pixel comparison qualifies geometry, illumination and measured coverage.

entries.subject: Released ADAM companion model
entries.finding: The live directory also lists 354_Eleonora_adam.obj. The body’s retained model comparison already distinguishes this ADAM reconstruction from the selected MPCD mesh. It is not adopted as a duplicate view of the same measured shape; the original comparison remains linked.
entries.revisitWhen: An observation or scientific comparison specifically requires this alternative mesh and its matching source frame.

entries.subject: VLT/SPHERE/ZIMPOL deconvolved frames as a computed-camera photograph lens
entries.finding: Measured on all 35 deconvolved frames with the release's rotation record, read latitude-first because 153.6484 degrees cannot be a latitude and both columns match DAMIT's 2021 model, cast onto the released ADAM mesh. The outline scores 24 of 35 frames and leaves 5.38 degrees after a 3.64-degree floor, outside the three-degree gate, so no lens ships. The disagreement is aspect-dependent rather than a constant error: restricted to the 11 frames whose outline reaches an elongation of 1.30, the residual is 1.31 degrees against a 1.35-degree floor, so where the outline defines a position angle at all the model agrees with it. Measured outside preparation by the registration stage's own modules (its limb fit, camera and caliper rule) driven from the pinned inputs, which reproduces Sylvia's prepared report to the digit (15 scored, rms 2.887, floor 1.871, systematic 2.198); on Themis it read 2.92 degrees where the stage itself read 1.65, so treat these as the rule applied to the frames, not as a prepared verdict.
entries.revisitWhen: A registration reference for this body: a spacecraft map, or a night whose frames hold an elongation above 1.30 across enough of a rotation for the outline alone to reach the gate.
